fields.title: Performance targets are stated and verified

sections.Purpose: Where performance matters, we say what "fast enough" means before we build, and we check against it before we release rather than discovering the answer from customers.
sections.Scope: Systems where throughput, latency, concurrency or capacity affect whether the system does its job, which is most customer-facing systems and many internal ones. Targets themselves are recorded as NFRs. This policy commits us to having them.
sections.Exceptions: Systems where performance is genuinely not a concern (low-volume internal tooling with no user waiting on it) need no targets. That judgement is a recorded deviation under [pol-DEVI], and its review date is what catches the system that has since acquired users.
